finalStep.prompt:
Your goal is to review the bug fixes from previous steps, then use append_step to
queue fixes for the bug reports currently in bugs/backlog.

You run as this workflow's final step. Every pass is a new session, so you have no
memory of earlier passes; the previous pass's output (if any) is attached above. Use
workflow_status and read_output for more detail.

## 1. Review the last round of fixes

Use workflow_status to find the steps that ran since the previous pass. If there are
none, skip to section 2. If a step only merged in another branch, don't review it as a
bug fix, but do account for what it brought in.

Review every bug fix that landed in that window (git log and the diffs). Confirm each
one actually fixes its bug, didn't introduce a regression, has test coverage, and moved
its bug report to bugs/implemented. Fix the problems you find and commit them. If a
follow-up is too big for this session, use append_step to queue it instead.

## 2. Queue the backlog

Read every bug report in bugs/backlog and the code it touches. Do not file new
bugs; this workflow only drains the existing backlog. If you notice a new bug while
reviewing, mention it in your summary instead.

If a report's description or suggested fix is clearly wrong, update the report first.
If a bug needs more thought than you can give it here, make finalizing it the first
queued step.

Then use append_step to add one step per chunk of work that can be completed in a
single session, ordered so fixes don't duplicate or conflict with each other. Group
small or related bugs into one step; split a really large fix into several. How you
split the work is your call; that judgment is the point of this workflow. Every queued
step must:
- be self-contained (it runs in a fresh session with none of your reasoning)
- name the bug report(s) it fixes
- add or update tests and pass `npm test`
- move each bug report it fixes to bugs/implemented (git mv) with a note that it
  was fixed in this commit
- commit its own work before finishing

If a bug needs my decision on the fix direction, skip it, queue the rest, and list it
in your summary with the decision you need from me. If every remaining bug is blocked
on me, queue nothing. If the backlog is empty and your review found nothing left to
fix, queue nothing; that ends the workflow.

End with a short summary: what you reviewed and fixed, what you queued, and anything
that needs my input.

You are running headless, so you can't ask questions. Use your best judgment, and if
you truly need my input, say so in your summary. When your turn ends your process
stops and kills any subprocesses you started, so don't end your turn to wait on a
task; block on long-running commands such as `npm test` instead, and stop any
server you started before you end your turn.
finalStep.name: drain-backlog
